title: The pursuit of happiness
abstract: arXiv:2506.10537v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper studies populations of individuals -- that we call homo-felix -- who maximise an objective function that we call happiness. The happiness of one individual depends on the payoffs that they receive in games they play with their peers as well as on the happiness of the peers they interact with, and on their status. Individuals care more or less about others depending on whether that makes them more or less happy. This paper analyses the ``happiness feedback loops'' that result from these interactions in simple settings. We find that individuals revise their other-regarding attitudes in terms of relative comparisons. In particular, individuals tend to care more about individuals who are happier than them, while spiteful behavior may emerge only under poor socio-economic conditions and is directed towards the worst off individuals. translated_abstract: 本文研究了一类个体种群——我们称之为“幸福人”——他们最大化一个我们称之为“幸福”的目标函数。一个个体的幸福取决于他们在与同伴博弈中获得的收益、他们所互动同伴的幸福，以及他们的地位。个体对他人的关心程度取决于这是否会让他们更快乐或更不快乐。本文分析了在简单环境中由这些互动产生的“幸福反馈回路”。我们发现，个体通过相对比较来修正自己关心他人的态度。特别地，个体往往更关心比自己更幸福的个体，而恶意（损人）行为只可能在糟糕的社会经济条件下出现，且指向境况最差的个体。这些一般性结论通过研究简单的2×2博弈加以说明，我们发现幸福人……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文构建了以“幸福”为目标的“幸福人”进化模型，通过幸福反馈回路分析发现：个体倾向于更关心比自己幸福的人，而恶意行为仅在糟糕的社会经济条件下才会出现，且指向境况最差的个体。
en_tdlr: This paper models "homo-felix" populations maximizing happiness through feedback loops, finding that individuals tend to care more about happier peers, while spiteful behavior emerges only under poor socio-economic conditions and is directed toward the worst-off individuals.
